subject: Post-call: Legal & Procurement routing (NDA → MSA/DPA) — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Collins <jared.collins@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Legal routing (NDA → MSA/DPA)

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Acme's roadmap and the priorities for the commerce platform team. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment on routing: 

Summary of needs
- Use-case: real-time product recommendations + conversational commerce (high qps, low 200–400ms P95).
- Decision criteria: latency under 300ms P95, predictable unit cost, on-prem data options for PCI scope.
- Timeline: target procurement decision by end of Q2 (preferred: 6/15).

Stakeholders you mentioned (please flag changes)
- Economic buyer: Samantha Lee (CPO)
- Security: Chris Nguyen (secops)
- Legal: Michelle Park (in-house counsel)
- Procurement: Robert Ames
- Day-to-day owner / technical contact: Jared Collins

Legal/routing ask
- To keep things moving we usually do: NDA executed → exchange MSA + DPA for redlines → procurement/PO.
- I've attached a standard mutual NDA for your legal team to review (Redwood-NDA-Acme-20260520.pdf).
- Can you confirm the preferred owners for NDA vs MSA/DPA, and whether procurement requires a PO or signed MSA first?

Proposed sequencing and turnaround expectations
1) NDA: goal to sign within 48–72 hours (if no material changes).
2) MSA + DPA: once NDA is in place, provide our MSA + DPA for legal redline. Typical external turn-times we've seen: initial redline 3–7 business days.
3) Procurement/PO: depends on your internal process (usually 3–10 business days after signed MSA).

Next steps
- Please confirm owners and whether we should route NDA to Michelle or procurement first.
- If helpful, I can loop in our Legal (Dev Patel) to speed the MSA/DPA exchange and pre-flag the clauses customers commonly change.

Attachments: Redwood-NDA-Acme-20260520.pdf (draft NDA)

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and we'll queue the next docs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Thanks Marissa — solid summary. Confirming stakeholders and routing from our side: 
- Economic buyer: Samantha Lee (CPO) — final signatory for budget.
- Legal owner for NDA/MSA/DPA: Michelle Park (in-house counsel) — I’ve CC'd her.
- Security review: Chris Nguyen — will validate PCI/data handling requirements; expect a short questionnaire.
- Procurement/PO: Robert Ames — he handles PO issuance and vendor onboarding.

Procurement note: they prefer a signed NDA before sharing certain internal architecture docs. For contract execution, procurement typically requires a signed MSA + DPA before issuing a PO; timeline varies but estimate 2–3 weeks from redline completion.

On the NDA — Michelle, can you please confirm if Acme has any standard language we should be aware of? If not, we'll review the attached NDA and aim to turn within 48–72 hours.

Also, Samantha — for budgeting, we’re aiming to have costs scoped this month; can you confirm if 6/15 still works as a decision target?

Thanks all — happy to coordinate next steps.

2) Once NDA is signed, we’ll send the MSA + DPA for your legal to redline.
3) Redwood legal (Dev) will prioritize an initial pass to align on data/IP clauses we commonly see changed.

- Redwood: initial legal review 48 business hours, full redline cycle 3–5 business days depending on complexity.
- External: we've observed 3–10 business days (procurement/enterprise legal varies).

- Please confirm if Acme requires a PO before work starts or if a confirmed signed MSA is sufficient.
- Would you prefer the MSA/DPA as Word with tracked changes or via DocuSign redlines? We can do either.

Subject: Redwood legal intake — next docs & redline expectations

Hi Michelle / Acme legal,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on stakeholder names — appreciate it. A few notes from Redwood legal to keep things moving: 

Documents we will send after NDA is executed:
- Redwood-MSA-v3.docx (MSA — standard for Hosted/Dedicated options)
- Redwood-DPA-v2.docx (Data Processing Addendum covering PCI/PII scoping)

Preferred format & redline process
- We prefer Word with tracked changes for MSA; DPA can be either tracked or a redline PDF.
- If you have a preferred template, please send it and we'll ingest changes.
- For speed, include a one-line summary of any high-priority changes (e.g., indemnity caps, data residency).

Turn-time expectations (internal)
- Initial Redwood review of your redline: 48 business hours for first pass.
- Full negotiation cycle: typically 3–7 business days for standard enterprisey redlines. More complex SOWs or custom IP clauses can add time.

Quick pre-flags (common asks we can pre-clear)
- We can be flexible on data residency commitments for scoped PCI workloads with an addendum.
- Standard indemnity and liability caps are negotiable within reason — if you have target numbers, share upfront.

Attachments included (for your convenience): Redwood-MSA-v3.docx, Redwood-DPA-v2.docx (stubs attached)

If you want, I can run a short 15–20m session with Michelle/Chris to walk through the clauses that usually drive back-and-forth.

Thanks — looking forward to the NDA sign and the MSA exchange.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
